Now let’s do twitter. 

Unironically, I’m curious, I know I’m addicted, although it’s thankfully the only social media exposure I’ve had for over three years now.
tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
Holy shit, I finally understand why nobody can quit Instagram. I've watched so many people delete it, swear they're done, and download it again a week later, me included. I always assumed it was a willpower problem. So I went down a rabbit hole to figure out what's actually going on inside the app, and I high key wasn't ready for what I found.

I came across a developer who took the Instagram app apart and went through its code. There are 40 AI models running directly on your phone, and a system that tracks 642 different things about you and your device. 

It knows your battery percentage and whether you're charging, which tells it whether you're settled in bed for the night or about to put your phone away. It checks whether your phone is running hot or in low power mode, so videos stay smooth, because a laggy video is one of the few natural reasons to close the app. 

It even knows your font size, whether you're in dark mode, whether you're wearing headphones and how loud your volume is, which is enough to tell if you're somewhere private, lying in the dark, or next to someone who's already asleep.

It watches how you scroll too. It counts every time you scroll back up to look at something again, which shows what really grabs you even when you never like the post. It counts every screenshot you take, because a screenshot means something mattered enough to keep. 

There's a timer for how long it's been since you last touched the app, and it keeps counting while your phone is asleep in your pocket, so it knows how long you can stay away and exactly what to show you the moment you come back. 

There's even a counter the code calls ad repetitive fatigue, which tracks how sick you are of an ad so it can be swapped out before you get annoyed enough to leave.

Then, when your phone asks for an ad in Reels, the request goes to something in the code called intent awareness ads, with all of these signals attached. So Instagram doesn't just know what you like. 

It knows the moment you're in. Low battery, lights off, headphones in, scrolling past midnight. An ad you'd skip without a thought at 2pm can land perfectly at 1am when you're tired and half asleep, and the app is built to tell those two moments apart.

We think Instagram is free because it has never asked us for money. But we pay with our time. The advertisers are the customers, our attention is what they're buying, and we are the product. So if you've ever been hard on yourself for not being able to put it down, go a little easier. It was never a willpower problem.

When they release a new model, you don't have to worry that they'll make it dumber in 2 weeks to save cost without telling anyone. They just leave it like it was launched

During peak hours, you don't have to worry about them quanting models or slowing inference down by 90% under load because they actually have enough compute to serve their customer

If you try and use a Google model for research, it will help you without 10 billion refusals/intentional sabotage.

Just a normal company that sells you normal products. Sounds basic but somehow in AI this is a high bar to meet
